name: PixMo-Count
intro: PixMo-Count 是 Molmo 与 PixMo 论文中的开放视觉计数数据集。论文v2以非VLM对象检测器处理网页图像，经严格置信度阈值后选择检测最多的类别，将对象中心作为点监督；固定数据卡进一步披露准确性与多样性过滤。计数2至10的样例按每个计数120条人工核验，形成各540条验证与测试集，其余0至10计数形成训练集。
org: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington
build_method: 非VLM Detic检测, 严格置信度阈值, 准确性与多样性过滤, 对象中心点, 人工核验评测集
metric: 精确计数Accuracy；固定代码另报close、valid与分计数正确率
task_type: 视觉计数问答, 对象中心点指点
eval_feature: 测试集主结果, 验证集四种计数策略消融, 计数任务12个图像裁剪, 固定PointCountEval解析器
scale: 论文约36k训练图像；固定发布36,916条训练、540条验证、540条测试
build_method_en: Non-VLM Detic detection, strict confidence thresholding, accuracy and diversity filtering, object-center supervision, human-verified evaluation splits
eval_feature_en: Held-out test results, four counting-strategy ablations on validation, 12 image crops for counting, pinned PointCountEval parser
intro_en: PixMo-Count is the open visual counting dataset introduced with Molmo and PixMo. Paper v2 applies a non-VLM object detector to web images, selects the most-detected class after strict confidence thresholding, and turns object centers into point supervision; the fixed dataset card additionally discloses accuracy and diversity filtering. For counts 2 through 10, 120 examples per count are manually verified and divided into 540 validation and 540 test rows. Remaining counts from 0 through 10 form the training split.
scale_en: Paper: about 36k training images; fixed release: 36,916 train, 540 validation, 540 test rows
metric_en: Exact-count Accuracy; pinned code also reports close, valid, and per-count correctness

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; scope=source-stage academic-paper Build Process reconstruction for PixMo-Count, with the paper defining construction and evaluation semantics and fixed official snapshots used only to verify released data and code behavior. The primary paper is pinned to https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17146v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.17146v2; paper-v2-pdf-sha256=54c5e78b4066eef960af1c108d758311b479879b6ba4215570e1c23f5f55510d. The official Molmo code snapshot is https://github.com/allenai/molmo/tree/793fa387edfd6fd0f5b21eb8e0a7620a1f3799e1 with tree=0a9e0c70f5b6253b8350c5b2273fa74c907d1f0f, README sha256=ea8cb2a8791e43ee86bf1c09224b03ad4b6378dc122cd809426a839d25917098, olmo/data/pixmo_datasets.py sha256=19dccee91d56c7afcd07268e0d448bc570856ed8f2325d5b594b8c800ff90b65, and olmo/eval/evaluators.py sha256=836d61f292c9da863a87ae1cf80c60089a85933f59a961b9d79e3260c3d846d9. The official data snapshot is https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/pixmo-count/tree/ebf51cf70e45d12374e64d475862e4f8d21d31d0 with tree=6c4b4b02abf1042b437348ac6deac84fbc3fb0ce and README sha256=91ed6ebcbb1ad47e35efd4e110e9ee29bc68bf9eafd841445c78226c53dd3538. The three fixed Parquet LFS object identifiers are train=e7f1c18ea69ed24e0842c55c7ec7de262d3cf3184847726f85c8d6e44b58b507, validation=006152a56c475603db4f7f8348e661697f3324565fee3e657efd8d4a0272dac1, and test=7be18afda3f91019829548c216afe436f371098342050a4f2b834b57372b1470. Paper-v2 Section 3 says PixMo-Count starts from web images and a standard non-VLM object detector, cited to the Detic work. For each image it selects the class with the most detections after strict confidence thresholding, turns selected detections into object-center points, and creates an image and counting-QA pair. The official dataset card independently names Detic and says the generated data was filtered to improve accuracy and diversity. The graph keeps those two levels of disclosure separate: strict confidence and dominant-class selection are paper facts, while the broad accuracy/diversity pass is a release-card fact. The paper does not identify the web-image corpus used for PixMo-Count, so the diagram does not borrow the approximately 70-topic acquisition description from PixMo-Cap. It also does not disclose the Detic checkpoint or detector configuration, the numerical confidence threshold, the accuracy or diversity rule implementation, source sampling weights, rejection counts, the allocation algorithm for the equal validation and test splits, or a split seed. The pinned Molmo repository contains a released dataset loader, training formatter, evaluation launcher, and PointCountEval but no reconstruction script for the Detic data-creation pipeline. These missing public components are explicitly marked undisclosed rather than inferred. For evaluation data, paper v2 follows CountBenchQA and manually verifies 120 samples for every count from 2 through 10. Nine count values times 120 gives 1,080 verified examples, which the paper reports as validation and test sets of 540 images each. The graph preserves that disclosed arithmetic without inventing a per-count randomization or assignment procedure. The remaining samples with counts from 0 through 10 form a paper-scale training set of about 36k images, each carrying object-center points and a QA pair. The fixed dataset card resolves the approximate paper count to exactly 36,916 training rows, 540 validation rows, and 540 test rows. Its schema is image_url, image_sha256, count, points with x and y, and label. It states that image URLs may repeat, images are downloaded separately, SHA-256 verifies downloaded bytes, and points are missing from the two evaluation splits. The release is ODC-BY-1.0 under the Ai2 Responsible Use Guidelines. The card metadata arxiv:2201.02605 refers to Detic, not the Molmo and PixMo paper, so the detail page pins arXiv:2409.17146v2 directly and does not treat the card tag as the benchmark paper. Paper Table 1 reports PixMo-Count held-out test Accuracy. Paper Table 4 calls the validation split PCQA and compares four counting strategies: count only 80.2, point then count 86.3, count then point 77.6, and pointing plus regular-expression count 85.4. The paper identifies point then count as the default and best of those branches and further reports that top-down, left-to-right point order is better than unordered points. The pointing-plus-regex ablation counts emitted point coordinates with the paper regex and does not pass that branch through PointCountEval text-count parsing. The main evaluation setup uses 12 crops for counting tasks because changing only the inference crop count harms pointing and counting; the appendix reports the 12-to-36 mismatch effect separately. At the pinned Git revision, PixMoCount loads the official validation, test, and train splits; it attaches points only for train and selects the point_count formatter when counting is enabled. The formatter exposes multiple prompt templates rather than one paper-fixed evaluation prompt. The downstream launcher evaluates pixmo_count_counting on validation or test and selects PointCountEval. That evaluator lowercases and trims output, attempts the final token as an integer or number word, then accepts the phrase a total of N. It reports exact correct, within-one close, parse-valid, and per-reference-count correctness. The diagram treats exact correctness as the benchmark Accuracy and the other fields as code diagnostics, not additional paper metrics. The Molmo README says VLMEvalKit support does not include PixMo-Count. The paper and fixed assets also do not pin a single randomized prompt choice, evaluation seed, model checkpoint for every reported external baseline, or an independent official evaluator package outside Molmo. Those reproduction limits remain dashed evidence boundaries. No Gemini Robotics provenance, hidden human relabeling stage, guessed detector threshold, or guessed diversity algorithm is introduced.
